summary: Intermittent 5xx wave from TLS-resume-ticket exhaustion combined with HTTP/2 negotiation mismatch between API gateway and runtime
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC NimbusHealth observed repeated 5xx errors for short periods (~2-8 minutes) across multiple chat and embedding routes. The API gateway returned 502/503 and upstream serving runtimes reported rapid connection resets and ephemeral worker evictions. Impact: customer-facing requests intermittently failed (up to 18% error rate during the peak window) causing degraded application experience for their enterprise workflows. Environment: production (us-east), mixed-hosted and dedicated tenant; incident coincided with a tenant priority reconfiguration from NimbusHealth account team.
impact: External: NimbusHealth experienced elevated 5xx rates across chat and embeddings endpoints, occasional streaming disconnects. Internal: apigw saw accept_queue growth and increased TLS handshake latency; several runtime pods restarted due to connection churn leading to transient capacity reduction.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a high-concurrency client to open many short-lived streaming connections (keepalive disabled) to chat route for NimbusHealth tenant. 2) Trigger a tenant priority reshuffle via admin console (simulate same weight/priority change). 3) Observe TLS handshake errors in apigw and intermittent 502/503 responses. Note: reproduces reliably when TLS ticket rate is high and client keepalives are low.
logs: apigw logs: repeated 'tls: session ticket cache exhausted' and 'http2: stream aborted before response received' entries. Runtime logs: 'connection reset by peer' followed by 'ephemeral-worker eviction: rapid reconnects' and short crashes of the runtime proxy. Metrics: accept_queue length spiked to 85% of capacity; TLS handshake p95 increased from 30ms to 420ms during bursts. Traces: distributed tracing shows HTTP/2 GOAWAYs issued from apigw immediately followed by runtime side aborts.
investigation_notes: Timeline: 09:12 first error spike, 09:15 escalation to SRE, 09:20 mitigation rollouts started. Hypothesis 1: TLS session-ticket exhaustion combined with apigw HTTP/2 SETTINGS window tweaks caused protocol negotiation mismatch and connection churn. Evidence: ticket-rotation metrics show burst of ticket invalidations at 09:10; apigw telemetry shows aggressive SETTINGS frame changes pushed during tenant reshuffle (window size and max_concurrent_streams altered). Hypothesis 2: Clients opening many short streams without keepalive force apigw to issue new TLS handshakes, exhausting the ticket cache and preventing fast resume, which amplifies handshake latency and triggers hedged-retries and hedged-retry loops. Partial findings: reproducer in staging confirmed ticket-cache exhaustion reproduces error pattern; disabling SETTINGS window change removed the GOAWAYs in test. Cross-references: related to earlier incidents about handshake-throttle and keepalive-cull (see linked issues).
comments: 2026-03-10 09:23 - Support (Ava): Customer reported error spikes and shared initial request ids and timestamps. Asked for logs and whether they had changed client-side keepalive settings.

2026-03-10 09:37 - SRE (Diego): Observed TLS ticket rotation metrics matching spike; created temporary alert to track ticket cache saturation. Started investigating apigw HTTP/2 settings pushed in the last config roll.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Eng (Priya S.): Confirmed apigw config change that nudges SETTINGS initial_window_size and max_concurrent_streams during tenant priority reshuffle. Reverted the SETTINGS tweak in Canary, seeing immediate reduction in GOAWAYs.

2026-03-10 10:25 - Support (Ava): Updated NimbusHealth that we are rolling a targeted mitigation and requested they test. Customer reported partial improvement but still small blips for heavy short-lived streams.

2026-03-10 11:00 - SRE (Diego): Deployed a two-part mitigation: 1) temporarily increase TLS session-ticket cache, 2) pin HTTP/2 SETTINGS for apigw-to-runtime connections to stable values during tenant reshuffles. Monitoring shows 5xx rate dropped below 1%.
resolution: Mitigation applied: increased apigw session-ticket cache size and pinned HTTP/2 SETTINGS for gateway->runtime control plane to prevent dynamic window resizing during tenant priority operations. Hotfix PRs merged: PR/7842 pinned SETTINGS and added a guard to skip SETTINGS updates during ticket-rotation windows; PR/1911 increased ticket cache and added metrics to alert earlier. Customer was informed and confirmed errors fell back to baseline. Triage: incident classified Sev1/P1; no customer data exposure.
resolution_notes: Hotfix rollout timeline: 2026-03-10 10:45 canary change; 2026-03-10 11:15 global rollout completed. Post-mitigation monitoring for 48 hours; no recurrence in the observed window. Root cause: interplay of intensive TLS ticket rotation (due to high short-lived connections and low keepalive) + dynamic HTTP/2 SETTINGS adjustments during tenant priority reshuffle causing frequent GOAWAYs and runtime evictions.
follow_up_tasks: Create a dedicated e2e test that simulates tenant priority reshuffles under high short-lived stream load (owner: SRE, due: 2026-03-24)
Add alerting for TLS session-ticket cache utilization crossing 70% (owner: infra-monitoring, due: 2026-03-18)
Add a configuration guard to avoid SETTINGS frame changes when ticket-rotation or high handshake latency is detected (owner: api-gateway team, due: 2026-03-20)
Document client guidance for enterprise customers: recommend keepalive configuration to reduce full TLS handshakes (owner: Solutions, due: 2026-03-22)
